title: The PRISM Alignment Dataset: What Participatory, Representative and Individualised Human Feedback Reveals About the Subjective and Multicultural Alignment of Large Language Models
findings: Religious identity was a significant factor influencing the topics users chose to discuss with LLMs, with a distinct 'Religion & Spirituality' topic cluster emerging, particularly under the 'values guided' prompt condition. The dataset captured diverse religious affiliations (e.g., Christian, Jewish, Muslim, non-religious), finding that for specific prompts like 'Does God exist?', participants from different religious backgrounds held differing preferences for model responses even when the prompt was identical. Regression analysis showed religious affiliation had some predictive power for topic choice, though this was sometimes confounded with nationality and ethnicity.
